text.p: Chemring Group Plc said on Friday that it will have a loss before tax and exceptional items of no more than two million stg in the half year.

The company said in a statement that sales in the six months to March 1997, will be around 31 million stg compared with 40.9 million previously. It made a profit of 4.5 million in the six months to March 1996.
It said that the group has continued to experience deferment of defence orders, which is hitting its UK-based defence businesses.
Chemring also said that it is experiencing difficulties with its specialist clothing division.
It expects to return to profit in the second half of the year, although it said profit before tax and exceptional items will be considerably lower than last year.
The firm will take an exceptional charge of eight million stg and write off related goodwill of 3.5 million in its interim results as part of its strategy to lower operating costs and reduce debt.
Half year results for the company are due on June 11 and the firm expects to reduce its dividend payout to 2p from 3.76p previously.
